solstice-sre: Hey team, we started seeing a spike of 429s and tail latency from our Dedicated pool at 11:05 UTC. Looks correlated with a batch of long-context requests from our webhook workers (avg 18k tokens). Noticed a ton of KV evictions and slab compaction logs. Can you help triage?

support_jess: Thanks — can you paste the error sample and any request IDs? Also which Deployment/cluster is this hitting?

solstice-sre: Hitting dedicated-prod-eu-2 (pool-id: dp-eu-2-7). Example error from client: `POST /v1/generate -> 429: rate_limit` but server logs show `kvcache_eviction: slab_reclaim=high, fragments=0.63, long_context_hits=0.92`. One request id: req_202309-8a1f. We're seeing sustained evict rate ~ 350/s.

solstice-sre: Quick repro steps: 1) send 10 concurrent requests, each context ~ 16k-20k tokens, 2) model = gptx-open-3b-quant, 3) batch_size=8 at client. Sample curl: ```
curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -d '{"model":"gptx-open-3b-quant","input":"<16k tokens>"}'
```

eng-runtime-ryan: Putting on our radar. Long KV contexts + high concurrency -> heavy KV growth and fragmentation. Do you have per-instance kvcache size metrics? Also any recent model swaps or quant changes?

solstice-sre: No model swap. We recently increased per-worker concurrency in our batcher (from 4->8) last deploy. kvcache.size_avg per node is ~ 28GB of 32GB configured; reclaim cycles spike when avg_context_len > 12k.

ops-lin: @eng-runtime-ryan quick mitigation you can ask customer: reduce client batch_size to 2-4 and / or chunk prompts (prefix cache won't help with whole 16k unique contexts). Could also temporarily pin to a smaller concurrency pool or lower per-node token_window.

eng-runtime-ryan: Agreed. Also want to see eviction trace: please gather `kvcache.evictions_per_min`, `kvcache.fragmentation_ratio`, `slab.reclaim_cycles` for last 30m and paste here. If fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 we should consider slab-compaction throttle adjustments.

solstice-sre: Pasting latest metrics snippet: ```
kvcache.evictions_per_min = 352
kvcache.fragmentation_ratio = 0.61
slab.reclaim_cycles = 18m
long_context_hit_rate = 0.89
queue_latency_p95 = 420ms
```

support_jess: Noted. Escalating to dedicated runtime oncall. Scheduling a quick call in 15m. Also flagged billing team in case customer sees billing anomalies.

sre-bot: ALERT: DedicatedPool dp-eu-2-7 kvcache.fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 (since 11:02 UTC). Incident ID INC-2024-772.

eng-runtime-ryan: Thanks — assigning to eng-runtime oncall. Initial hypothesis: noisy long-context tenant causing KV slab churn and high fragmentation -> reclaim cycles thrash -> eviction storms -> token-serving backpressure -> 429s. We can try: 1) temporary per-tenant eviction throttle (lower eviction burst cap), 2) move Solstice to warm standby nodes with empty caches, or 3) pin to model variant with smaller kv footprint (if available).

ops-lin: Also check autoscaler behavior: if the autoscaler is slow to add nodes because reclaiming freed memory takes time, capacity will lag. If autoscale cooldowns are long, that makes the evict+429 loop worse.

solstice-sre: We'll immediately roll batcher concurrency back to 3 and start chunking contexts. I'll upload request traces (req_202309-8a1f + req_202309-8a2d) in the incident ticket.

support_jess: Perfect. Once you revert client change, ping here. We'll monitor eviction and 429s. If we still see >200 evictions/min after 10m, eng-runtime will apply temporary per-tenant cap.

eng-runtime-ryan: For follow-up, please include a few core dumps from nodes showing slab allocator stats (if safe), and we may run a quick compact-to-zero cycle during low traffic window.

solstice-sre: Understood. Thanks all. Will update in 10m after changes. :thumbsup:
